pairs: How to find papers worth reading on Google Scholar
Real search: "generative AI" "tutoring"; limited to 2024-2025, look at the first 10 results first.
The first report was cited 204 times;
The first 10 items are saved as CSV;
Check the version relationship item by item.

Source: Utah CS5493/6493, 2026, pp.35, 41, 52; Google Scholar official search help; Google Scholar actual page, 2026-10-19; Bai et al., GPTutor original text and corrections
items.note:
Use a real Google Scholar page to demonstrate how to start a search from a question. In this round, the search terms "generative AI" and "tutoring" are opened in the built-in browser. The year is limited to 2024-2025. The first 10 items in the list, screenshots and page records are actually saved. The default ordering is by relevance, and the first article cannot be called the most cited paper in the entire field. The screenshot is partially enlarged to retain the search terms, year, first two results and citations. The complete original image is retained with the package, and the numbers are not modified. The reading date of the citations is October 19, 2026. The page approximation is not regarded as the whole database data, and it is not exported in batches.
Let’s look at the material type first. The first article has 204 citations. Returning to the arXiv title and abstract, the author marked it as a report; the abstract introduces applications and challenges and cannot be regarded as a student effect experiment. Article 2 has 65 citations. Returning to the original journal title and abstract shows that it is a systematic review. Article 4 has been cited 31 times. In the original text of GPTutor, it can be seen that its research usage records and participation cannot be directly written as a causal improvement in independent answering ability. The sample responded from 880 responses to 741 eligible people, and then to 727 final analysts. If you write the results, you must use the corresponding denominator; correct and supplement the author contribution statement. The scope of the original text review was registered item by item. The first 10 articles were not completely read, and the other 7 items were still unverified candidate materials.
Then check the version. Calo and MacLellan's arXiv text are clearly related to the conference DOI, which belongs to the same working version relationship that was actually verified in this lesson. The two GPTutor titles cannot be automatically merged simply because they have the same name in the system. Whether the conference and journal research are duplicated still needs to be verified. The merging basis and pending matters are saved in version deduplication judgment.csv. Then compare it with the public technical plan, method diagram and learning test materials on page 10 to distinguish how the system does it, how involved it is, and whether it can answer independently after removing the AI. Different results cannot be combined into the same effect.
The user has agreed to replace Web of Science with an accessible academic portal. This page does not pretend to use WoS highly cited tags, does not treat Google Scholar citations as a normalized quality score, and does not predict future hot spots based on 10 results. Only one real search, file preservation, and limited original text checking are demonstrated here; there are no independent model full database search pipelines, systematic reviews, or new experiments. The Chinese explanations are written by AI and are yet to be reviewed by the teacher. Page 41 of Utah2026 continues to serve as a reference based on the teaching sequence of classifying existing work and then identifying problems. This page will be reviewed again this time.

A Turkish high school mathematics study measured practice scores with AI assistance and independent tests without assistance.
Tutor: Contains preset prompts for teachers.
Compared with the control group without AI,
Base group was 17% lower than the control.
The difference between Tutor group and control was not significant.

Chart: With AI help, the improvement of practice performance compared to the control group (barChart):
items.note:
The study was conducted in a high school in Türkiye, and three groups were randomly assigned according to classes: no generative AI resources, GPT Base, and GPT Tutor. What is redrawn here is the relative improvement of 48% and 127% in the summary report's practice scores compared to the control group, not the correct rate or percentage points, and no confidence intervals are drawn. Table 1 of the original article reports that the practice effects are 0.137 and 0.361, and the comparison mean is 0.284; the percentages in the original article are rounded. In the test after removing resources, the Base score was 17% lower than that of the control group; the difference between Tutor and the control group did not reach statistical significance, and it cannot be said that the two groups are exactly the same. This shows that the topic selection must make it clear how to "learn" to measure. This page is a numerical summary of the original article, its images are not reproduced.

pairs: Different questions can be asked on the same topic. The evidence required changes with the question.
In what tasks do teachers use AI?
Which students are more likely to be over-dependent?
Estimating the difference due to intervention
There are also mechanistic, explanatory, and qualitative issues; these three categories are used to illustrate common evidence differences.
Source: Tello-Trillo, 2026, text version of the author’s courseware; course teaching simulation/method description
items.note:
The description problem is concerned with what happened and its distribution; the prediction problem is concerned with whether unobserved results can be predicted; the causal problem is concerned with the difference that changing a condition will bring. Predicting accurately does not automatically equal finding the cause. Qualitative research can explore experiences, meanings and processes and cannot shoehorn into quantitative causal models. The examples on this page are teaching simulations and do not represent real teacher surveys or trained models.
